  15    def get_shortest_path_tree(
  16        self,
  17        origin_id: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float],
  18    ) -> dict:
  19        """
  20        Function:
  21
  22        - Calculate the shortest path tree of a graph using Dijkstra's algorithm
  23
  24        Required Arguments:
  25
  26        - `origin_id`
  27            - Type: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float]
  28            - What: The id(s) of the node(s) (with optional starting distances) from which to calculate the shortest path tree
  29
  30        Returns:
  31
  32        - A dictionary with the following keys:
  33            - `origin_id`: The id of the node from which the shortest path tree was calculated
  34            - `predecessors`: A list of node ids referring to the predecessor of each node given the shortest path tree
  35                - Note: For disconnected graphs, nodes that are not connected to the origin node will have a predecessor of None
  36            - `distance_matrix`: A list of distances from the origin node to each node in the graph
  37                - Note: For disconnected graphs, nodes that are not connected to the origin node will have a distance of float("inf")
  38
  39        """
  40        # Input Validation
  41        self.__input_check__(origin_id=origin_id, destination_id=0)
  42        origin_dict = normalize_node_input(origin_id)
  43
  44        # Variable Initialization
  45        graph = self.graph
  46        distance_matrix = [float("inf")] * len(graph)
  47        open_leaves = []
  48        predecessor = [-1] * len(graph)
  49
  50        for oid, odist in origin_dict.items():
  51            distance_matrix[oid] = odist
  52            heappush(open_leaves, (odist, oid))
  53
  54        while open_leaves:
  55            current_distance, current_id = heappop(open_leaves)
  56            for connected_id, connected_distance in graph[current_id].items():
  57                possible_distance = current_distance + connected_distance
  58                if possible_distance < distance_matrix[connected_id]:
  59                    distance_matrix[connected_id] = possible_distance
  60                    predecessor[connected_id] = current_id
  61                    heappush(open_leaves, (possible_distance, connected_id))
  62
  63        return {
  64            "origin_id": origin_id,
  65            "predecessors": predecessor,
  66            "distance_matrix": distance_matrix,
  67        }

  69    def get_tree_path(
  70        self,
  71        origin_id: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float],
  72        destination_id: int,
  73        tree_data: dict,
  74        length_only: bool = False,
  75    ) -> dict:
  76        """
  77        Function:
  78
  79        - Get the path from the origin node to the destination node using the provided tree_data
  80        - Return a list of node ids in the order they are visited as well as the length of the path
  81        - If the destination node is not reachable from the origin node, return None
  82
  83        Required Arguments:
  84
  85        - `origin_id`
  86            - Type: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float]
  87            - What: The id of the origin node from the graph dictionary to start the shortest path from
  88            - Note: Since multiple origins are possible, if the origin_id is not a predecessor node of the destination node, the closest origin will be used.
  89        - `destination_id`
  90            - Type: int
  91            - What: The id of the destination node from the graph dictionary to end the shortest path at
  92        - `tree_data`
  93            - Type: dict
  94            - What: The output from a tree function
  95
  96        Optional Arguments:
  97
  98        - `length_only`
  99            - Type: bool
 100            - What: If True, only returns the length of the path
 101            - Default: False
 102
 103        Returns:
 104
 105        - A dictionary with the following keys:
 106            - `path`: A list of node ids in the order they are visited from the origin node to the destination node
 107            - `length`: The length of the path from the origin node to the destination node
 108        """
 109        origin_dict = normalize_node_input(origin_id)
 110        tree_orig_dict = normalize_node_input(tree_data["origin_id"])
 111
 112        start_dist = 0.0
 113        if len(tree_orig_dict) == 1:
 114            tree_root = next(iter(tree_orig_dict.keys()))
 115            if tree_root not in origin_dict:
 116                raise Exception(
 117                    "The origin node must be the same as the spanning node for this function to work."
 118                )
 119            start_dist = origin_dict[tree_root] - tree_orig_dict[tree_root]
 120
 121        dest_dict = normalize_node_input(destination_id)
 122        best_dist = float("inf")
 123        best_dest_node = -1
 124        for did, ddist in dest_dict.items():
 125            if tree_data["distance_matrix"][did] < float("inf"):
 126                tot = start_dist + tree_data["distance_matrix"][did] + ddist
 127                if tot < best_dist:
 128                    best_dist = tot
 129                    best_dest_node = did
 130
 131        if best_dest_node == -1 or best_dist == float("inf"):
 132            raise Exception(
 133                "Something went wrong, the origin and destination nodes are not connected."
 134            )
 135        if length_only:
 136            return {"path": [], "length": best_dist}
 137        current_id = best_dest_node
 138        current_path = [best_dest_node]
 139        while current_id != -1 and tree_data["predecessors"][current_id] != -1:
 140            current_id = tree_data["predecessors"][current_id]
 141            current_path.append(current_id)
 142        current_path.reverse()
 143        return {
 144            "path": current_path,
 145            "length": best_dist,
 146        }

 149class GraphAlgorithms:
 150    @algorithm
 151    def dijkstra(
 152        self,
 153        origin_id: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float],
 154        destination_id: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float],
 155    ) -> dict:
 156        """
 157        Function:
 158
 159        - Identify the shortest path between two nodes in a sparse network graph using a modified Dijkstra algorithm
 160
 161        - Return a dictionary of various path information including:
 162            - `path`: A list of node ids in the order they are visited
 163            - `length`: The length of the path from the origin node to the destination node
 164
 165        Required Arguments:
 166
 167        - `origin_id`
 168            - Type: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float]
 169            - What: The id(s) of the origin node(s) (with optional starting distances) from the graph dictionary to start the shortest path from
 170        - `destination_id`
 171            - Type: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float]
 172            - What: The id(s) of the destination node(s) (with optional exit distances) from the graph dictionary to end the shortest path at
 173
 174        Optional Arguments:
 175
 176        - None
 177        """
 178        # Input Validation
 179        self.__input_check__(origin_id=origin_id, destination_id=destination_id)
 180        origin_dict = normalize_node_input(origin_id)
 181        dest_dict = normalize_node_input(destination_id)
 182
 183        # Variable Initialization
 184        graph = self.graph
 185        distance_matrix = [float("inf")] * len(graph)
 186        predecessor = [-1] * len(graph)
 187        open_leaves = []
 188
 189        for oid, odist in origin_dict.items():
 190            distance_matrix[oid] = odist
 191            heappush(open_leaves, (odist, oid))
 192
 193        best_dist = float("inf")
 194        best_dest_node = -1
 195        for did, ddist in dest_dict.items():
 196            if did in origin_dict:
 197                cand = origin_dict[did] + ddist
 198                if cand < best_dist:
 199                    best_dist = cand
 200                    best_dest_node = did
 201
 202        while open_leaves:
 203            current_distance, current_id = heappop(open_leaves)
 204            if current_distance >= best_dist:
 205                break
 206            if current_distance == distance_matrix[current_id]:
 207                if current_id in dest_dict:
 208                    cand = current_distance + dest_dict[current_id]
 209                    if cand < best_dist:
 210                        best_dist = cand
 211                        best_dest_node = current_id
 212                for connected_id, connected_distance in graph[
 213                    current_id
 214                ].items():
 215                    possible_distance = current_distance + connected_distance
 216                    if possible_distance < distance_matrix[connected_id]:
 217                        distance_matrix[connected_id] = possible_distance
 218                        predecessor[connected_id] = current_id
 219                        if connected_id in dest_dict:
 220                            cand = possible_distance + dest_dict[connected_id]
 221                            if cand < best_dist:
 222                                best_dist = cand
 223                                best_dest_node = connected_id
 224                        if possible_distance < best_dist:
 225                            heappush(
 226                                open_leaves, (possible_distance, connected_id)
 227                            )
 228
 229        if best_dest_node == -1 or best_dist == float("inf"):
 230            raise Exception(
 231                "Something went wrong, the origin and destination nodes are not connected."
 232            )
 233
 234        return {
 235            "path": self.__reconstruct_path__(best_dest_node, predecessor),
 236            "length": best_dist,
 237        }
 238
 239    @algorithm(bidirectional=True)
 240    def bidirectional_dijkstra(
 241        self,
 242        origin_id: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float],
 243        destination_id: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float],
 244    ) -> dict:
 245        """
 246        Function:
 247
 248        - Identify the shortest path between two nodes in a sparse network graph using a bidirectional Dijkstra algorithm
 249
 250        - Return a dictionary of various path information including:
 251            - `path`: A list of node ids in the order they are visited
 252            - `length`: The length of the path from the origin node to the destination node
 253
 254        Required Arguments:
 255
 256        - `origin_id`
 257            - Type: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float]
 258            - What: The id(s) of the origin node(s) (with optional starting distances) from the graph dictionary to start the shortest path from
 259        - `destination_id`
 260            - Type: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float]
 261            - What: The id(s) of the destination node(s) (with optional exit distances) from the graph dictionary to end the shortest path at
 262
 263        Optional Arguments:
 264
 265        - None
 266        """
 267        # Input Validation
 268        self.__input_check__(origin_id=origin_id, destination_id=destination_id)
 269        origin_dict = normalize_node_input(origin_id)
 270        dest_dict = normalize_node_input(destination_id)
 271        origin_ids = set(origin_dict.keys())
 272        dest_ids = set(dest_dict.keys())
 273
 274        self.__ensure_inverse_graph__()
 275
 276        graph = self.graph
 277        inverse_graph = self.inverse_graph
 278        num_nodes = len(graph)
 279
 280        forward_dist = [float("inf")] * num_nodes
 281        forward_pred = [-1] * num_nodes
 282        forward_open = []
 283
 284        backward_dist = [float("inf")] * num_nodes
 285        backward_pred = [-1] * num_nodes
 286        backward_open = []
 287
 288        best_dist = float("inf")
 289        meeting_node = -1
 290        inf = float("inf")
 291
 292        for oid, odist in origin_dict.items():
 293            forward_dist[oid] = odist
 294            heappush(forward_open, (odist, oid))
 295
 296        for did, ddist in dest_dict.items():
 297            backward_dist[did] = ddist
 298            heappush(backward_open, (ddist, did))
 299            if did in origin_dict:
 300                cand = origin_dict[did] + ddist
 301                if cand < best_dist:
 302                    best_dist = cand
 303                    meeting_node = did
 304
 305        while forward_open and backward_open:
 306            top_fwd = forward_open[0][0]
 307            top_bwd = backward_open[0][0]
 308            if top_fwd + top_bwd >= best_dist:
 309                break
 310
 311            if top_fwd <= top_bwd:
 312                cur_d, u = heappop(forward_open)
 313                if cur_d > forward_dist[u]:
 314                    continue
 315                for v, w in graph[u].items():
 316                    new_d = cur_d + w
 317                    if new_d < forward_dist[v]:
 318                        forward_dist[v] = new_d
 319                        forward_pred[v] = u
 320                        b_d = backward_dist[v]
 321                        if b_d < inf:
 322                            total_d = new_d + b_d
 323                            if total_d < best_dist:
 324                                best_dist = total_d
 325                                meeting_node = v
 326                        if new_d + top_bwd < best_dist:
 327                            heappush(forward_open, (new_d, v))
 328            else:
 329                cur_d, v = heappop(backward_open)
 330                if cur_d > backward_dist[v]:
 331                    continue
 332                for u, w in inverse_graph[v].items():
 333                    new_d = cur_d + w
 334                    if new_d < backward_dist[u]:
 335                        backward_dist[u] = new_d
 336                        backward_pred[u] = v
 337                        f_d = forward_dist[u]
 338                        if f_d < inf:
 339                            total_d = f_d + new_d
 340                            if total_d < best_dist:
 341                                best_dist = total_d
 342                                meeting_node = u
 343                        if new_d + top_fwd < best_dist:
 344                            heappush(backward_open, (new_d, u))
 345
 346        if meeting_node == -1 or best_dist == float("inf"):
 347            raise Exception(
 348                "Something went wrong, the origin and destination nodes are not connected."
 349            )
 350
 351        forward_path = []
 352        curr = meeting_node
 353        while curr != -1:
 354            forward_path.append(curr)
 355            if curr in origin_ids and forward_pred[curr] == -1:
 356                break
 357            curr = forward_pred[curr]
 358        forward_path.reverse()
 359
 360        backward_path = []
 361        curr = meeting_node
 362        while not (curr in dest_ids and backward_pred[curr] == -1):
 363            curr = backward_pred[curr]
 364            if curr != -1:
 365                backward_path.append(curr)
 366            else:
 367                break
 368
 369        return {
 370            "path": forward_path + backward_path,
 371            "length": best_dist,
 372        }

 374    @algorithm
 375    def dijkstra_buckets(
 376        self,
 377        origin_id: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float],
 378        destination_id: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float],
 379        max_edge_weight: int | float | None = None,
 380    ) -> dict:
 381        """
 382        Function:
 383
 384        - Identify the shortest path between two nodes in a sparse network graph using Dijkstra's algorithm with buckets (Dial's algorithm)
 385        - This is particularly efficient for graphs where most edge weights are >= 1 and the maximum edge weight is small
 386        - This implementation safely supports non-integer weights
 387        - Return a dictionary of various path information including:
 388            - `path`: A list of node ids in the order they are visited
 389            - `length`: The length of the path from the origin node to the destination node
 390
 391        Required Arguments:
 392
 393        - `origin_id`
 394            - Type: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float]
 395            - What: The id(s) of the origin node(s) (with optional starting distances) from the graph dictionary to start the shortest path from
 396        - `destination_id`
 397            - Type: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float]
 398            - What: The id(s) of the destination node(s) (with optional exit distances) from the graph dictionary to end the shortest path at
 399
 400        Optional Arguments:
 401
 402        - `max_edge_weight`
 403            - Type: int | float | None
 404            - What: The maximum edge weight in the graph. If None, it will be calculated.
 405            - Default: None
 406        """
 407        # Input Validation
 408        self.__input_check__(origin_id=origin_id, destination_id=destination_id)
 409        origin_dict = normalize_node_input(origin_id)
 410        dest_dict = normalize_node_input(destination_id)
 411        graph = self.graph
 412
 413        max_edge_weight = self.__get_max_edge_weight__(max_edge_weight)
 414
 415        # Variable Initialization
 416        distance_matrix = [float("inf")] * len(graph)
 417        predecessor = [-1] * len(graph)
 418        num_buckets = max_edge_weight + 1
 419        buckets = [[] for _ in range(num_buckets)]
 420
 421        for oid, odist in origin_dict.items():
 422            distance_matrix[oid] = odist
 423            buckets[int(odist) % num_buckets].append(oid)
 424
 425        current_dist = (
 426            min(int(odist) for odist in origin_dict.values())
 427            if origin_dict
 428            else 0
 429        )
 430        nodes_in_buckets = len(origin_dict)
 431
 432        best_dist = float("inf")
 433        best_dest_node = -1
 434        for did, ddist in dest_dict.items():
 435            if did in origin_dict:
 436                cand = origin_dict[did] + ddist
 437                if cand < best_dist:
 438                    best_dist = cand
 439                    best_dest_node = did
 440
 441        while nodes_in_buckets > 0:
 442            bucket_idx = current_dist % num_buckets
 443            while not buckets[bucket_idx]:
 444                current_dist += 1
 445                bucket_idx = current_dist % num_buckets
 446                if nodes_in_buckets == 0:
 447                    break
 448                # If we've already found a path shorter than the current bucket minimum, we can exit
 449                if best_dist < current_dist:
 450                    break
 451
 452            if nodes_in_buckets == 0 or best_dist < current_dist:
 453                break
 454
 455            current_id = buckets[bucket_idx].pop()
 456            nodes_in_buckets -= 1
 457
 458            # Skip if we found a better path already (lazy removal)
 459            if distance_matrix[current_id] < current_dist:
 460                continue
 461
 462            if current_id in dest_dict:
 463                cand = distance_matrix[current_id] + dest_dict[current_id]
 464                if cand < best_dist:
 465                    best_dist = cand
 466                    best_dest_node = current_id
 467
 468            for connected_id, connected_distance in graph[current_id].items():
 469                possible_distance = (
 470                    distance_matrix[current_id] + connected_distance
 471                )
 472                if possible_distance < distance_matrix[connected_id]:
 473                    distance_matrix[connected_id] = possible_distance
 474                    predecessor[connected_id] = current_id
 475                    if connected_id in dest_dict:
 476                        cand = possible_distance + dest_dict[connected_id]
 477                        if cand < best_dist:
 478                            best_dist = cand
 479                            best_dest_node = connected_id
 480                    buckets[int(possible_distance) % num_buckets].append(
 481                        connected_id
 482                    )
 483                    nodes_in_buckets += 1
 484
 485        if best_dest_node == -1 or best_dist == float("inf"):
 486            raise Exception(
 487                "Something went wrong, the origin and destination nodes are not connected."
 488            )
 489
 490        return {
 491            "path": self.__reconstruct_path__(best_dest_node, predecessor),
 492            "length": best_dist,
 493        }
 494
 495    @algorithm(bidirectional=True)
 496    def bidirectional_buckets(
 497        self,
 498        origin_id: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float],
 499        destination_id: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float],
 500        max_edge_weight: int | float | None = None,
 501    ) -> dict:
 502        """
 503        Function:
 504
 505        - Identify the shortest path between two nodes in a sparse network graph using a bidirectional Dijkstra algorithm with buckets (Dial's algorithm)
 506        - This is particularly efficient for graphs where most edge weights are >= 1 and the maximum edge weight is small
 507        - This implementation safely supports non-integer weights
 508        - Return a dictionary of various path information including:
 509            - `path`: A list of node ids in the order they are visited
 510            - `length`: The length of the path from the origin node to the destination node
 511
 512        Required Arguments:
 513
 514        - `origin_id`
 515            - Type: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float]
 516            - What: The id(s) of the origin node(s) (with optional starting distances) from the graph dictionary to start the shortest path from
 517        - `destination_id`
 518            - Type: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float]
 519            - What: The id(s) of the destination node(s) (with optional exit distances) from the graph dictionary to end the shortest path at
 520
 521        Optional Arguments:
 522
 523        - `max_edge_weight`
 524            - Type: int | float | None
 525            - What: The maximum edge weight in the graph. If None, it will be calculated.
 526            - Default: None
 527        """
 528        # Input Validation
 529        self.__input_check__(origin_id=origin_id, destination_id=destination_id)
 530        origin_dict = normalize_node_input(origin_id)
 531        dest_dict = normalize_node_input(destination_id)
 532        origin_ids = set(origin_dict.keys())
 533        dest_ids = set(dest_dict.keys())
 534
 535        self.__ensure_inverse_graph__()
 536
 537        graph = self.graph
 538        inverse_graph = self.inverse_graph
 539        num_nodes = len(graph)
 540
 541        max_edge_weight = self.__get_max_edge_weight__(max_edge_weight)
 542
 543        num_buckets = max_edge_weight + 1
 544        forward_dist = [float("inf")] * num_nodes
 545        forward_pred = [-1] * num_nodes
 546        forward_buckets = [[] for _ in range(num_buckets)]
 547
 548        backward_dist = [float("inf")] * num_nodes
 549        backward_pred = [-1] * num_nodes
 550        backward_buckets = [[] for _ in range(num_buckets)]
 551
 552        best_dist = float("inf")
 553        meeting_node = -1
 554        inf = float("inf")
 555
 556        for oid, odist in origin_dict.items():
 557            forward_dist[oid] = odist
 558            forward_buckets[int(odist) % num_buckets].append(oid)
 559
 560        for did, ddist in dest_dict.items():
 561            backward_dist[did] = ddist
 562            backward_buckets[int(ddist) % num_buckets].append(did)
 563            if did in origin_dict:
 564                cand = origin_dict[did] + ddist
 565                if cand < best_dist:
 566                    best_dist = cand
 567                    meeting_node = did
 568
 569        fwd_current_dist = (
 570            min(int(odist) for odist in origin_dict.values())
 571            if origin_dict
 572            else 0
 573        )
 574        bwd_current_dist = (
 575            min(int(ddist) for ddist in dest_dict.values()) if dest_dict else 0
 576        )
 577        fwd_nodes_in_buckets = len(origin_dict)
 578        bwd_nodes_in_buckets = len(dest_dict)
 579
 580        while fwd_nodes_in_buckets > 0 and bwd_nodes_in_buckets > 0:
 581            fwd_bucket_idx = fwd_current_dist % num_buckets
 582            while not forward_buckets[fwd_bucket_idx]:
 583                fwd_current_dist += 1
 584                fwd_bucket_idx = fwd_current_dist % num_buckets
 585                if fwd_nodes_in_buckets == 0:
 586                    break
 587                if fwd_current_dist + bwd_current_dist >= best_dist:
 588                    break
 589
 590            bwd_bucket_idx = bwd_current_dist % num_buckets
 591            while not backward_buckets[bwd_bucket_idx]:
 592                bwd_current_dist += 1
 593                bwd_bucket_idx = bwd_current_dist % num_buckets
 594                if bwd_nodes_in_buckets == 0:
 595                    break
 596                if fwd_current_dist + bwd_current_dist >= best_dist:
 597                    break
 598
 599            if (
 600                fwd_nodes_in_buckets == 0
 601                or bwd_nodes_in_buckets == 0
 602                or fwd_current_dist + bwd_current_dist >= best_dist
 603            ):
 604                break
 605
 606            if fwd_current_dist <= bwd_current_dist:
 607                u = forward_buckets[fwd_bucket_idx].pop()
 608                fwd_nodes_in_buckets -= 1
 609
 610                if forward_dist[u] < fwd_current_dist:
 611                    continue
 612
 613                cur_d = forward_dist[u]
 614                for v, w in graph[u].items():
 615                    new_d = cur_d + w
 616                    if new_d < forward_dist[v]:
 617                        forward_dist[v] = new_d
 618                        forward_pred[v] = u
 619                        b_d = backward_dist[v]
 620                        if b_d < inf:
 621                            total_d = new_d + b_d
 622                            if total_d < best_dist:
 623                                best_dist = total_d
 624                                meeting_node = v
 625                        if new_d + bwd_current_dist < best_dist:
 626                            forward_buckets[int(new_d) % num_buckets].append(v)
 627                            fwd_nodes_in_buckets += 1
 628            else:
 629                v = backward_buckets[bwd_bucket_idx].pop()
 630                bwd_nodes_in_buckets -= 1
 631
 632                if backward_dist[v] < bwd_current_dist:
 633                    continue
 634
 635                cur_d = backward_dist[v]
 636                for u, w in inverse_graph[v].items():
 637                    new_d = cur_d + w
 638                    if new_d < backward_dist[u]:
 639                        backward_dist[u] = new_d
 640                        backward_pred[u] = v
 641                        f_d = forward_dist[u]
 642                        if f_d < inf:
 643                            total_d = f_d + new_d
 644                            if total_d < best_dist:
 645                                best_dist = total_d
 646                                meeting_node = u
 647                        if new_d + fwd_current_dist < best_dist:
 648                            backward_buckets[int(new_d) % num_buckets].append(u)
 649                            bwd_nodes_in_buckets += 1
 650
 651        if meeting_node == -1 or best_dist == float("inf"):
 652            raise Exception(
 653                "Something went wrong, the origin and destination nodes are not connected."
 654            )
 655
 656        forward_path = []
 657        curr = meeting_node
 658        while curr != -1:
 659            forward_path.append(curr)
 660            if curr in origin_ids and forward_pred[curr] == -1:
 661                break
 662            curr = forward_pred[curr]
 663        forward_path.reverse()
 664
 665        backward_path = []
 666        curr = meeting_node
 667        while not (curr in dest_ids and backward_pred[curr] == -1):
 668            curr = backward_pred[curr]
 669            if curr != -1:
 670                backward_path.append(curr)
 671            else:
 672                break
 673
 674        return {
 675            "path": forward_path + backward_path,
 676            "length": best_dist,
 677        }
 678
 679    @algorithm
 680    def dijkstra_negative(
 681        self,
 682        origin_id: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float],
 683        destination_id: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float],
 684        cycle_check_iterations: int | None = None,
 685    ) -> dict:
 686        """
 687        Function:
 688
 689        - Identify the shortest path between two nodes in a sparse network graph using a modified Dijkstra algorithm that catches negative cycles
 690            - Negative cycles raise an exception if they are detected
 691        - Note: This algorithm is guaranteed to find the shortest path or raise an exception if a negative cycle is detected
 692        - Note: This algorithm requires computing the entire shortest path tree of the graph and is therefore not able to be terminated early
 693            - For non negative weighted graphs, it is recommended to use the `dijkstra` algorithm instead
 694        - Note: This should be fairly performant in general, however it does have a higher worst-case time complexity than Bellman-Ford
 695
 696        - Return a dictionary of various path information including:
 697            - `id_path`: A list of node ids in the order they are visited
 698            - `path`: A list of node dictionaries (lat + long) in the order they are visited
 699
 700        Required Arguments:
 701
 702        - `origin_id`
 703            - Type: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float]
 704            - What: The id(s) of the origin node(s) (with optional starting distances) from the graph dictionary to start the shortest path from
 705        - `destination_id`
 706            - Type: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float]
 707            - What: The id(s) of the destination node(s) (with optional exit distances) from the graph dictionary to end the shortest path at
 708
 709        Optional Arguments:
 710
 711        - `cycle_check_iterations`
 712            - Type: int | None
 713            - What: The number of iterations to loop over before checking for negative cycles
 714            - Default: None (Then set to the number of nodes in the graph)
 715        """
 716        # Input Validation
 717        self.__input_check__(origin_id=origin_id, destination_id=destination_id)
 718        origin_dict = normalize_node_input(origin_id)
 719        dest_dict = normalize_node_input(destination_id)
 720        graph = self.graph
 721
 722        # Variable Initialization
 723        distance_matrix = [float("inf")] * len(graph)
 724        predecessor = [-1] * len(graph)
 725        open_leaves = []
 726
 727        for oid, odist in origin_dict.items():
 728            distance_matrix[oid] = odist
 729            heappush(open_leaves, (odist, oid))
 730
 731        # Cycle iteration Variables
 732        cycle_iteration = 0
 733        if cycle_check_iterations is None:
 734            cycle_check_iterations = len(graph)
 735
 736        while open_leaves:
 737            current_distance, current_id = heappop(open_leaves)
 738            if current_distance == distance_matrix[current_id]:
 739                # Increment the cycle iteration counter and check for negative cycles if the iteration limit is reached
 740                cycle_iteration += 1
 741                if cycle_iteration >= cycle_check_iterations:
 742                    cycle_iteration = 0  # Reset the cycle iteration counter
 743                    self.__check_predecessor_loop__(
 744                        predecessor_matrix=predecessor, node_id=current_id
 745                    )
 746                for connected_id, connected_distance in graph[
 747                    current_id
 748                ].items():
 749                    possible_distance = current_distance + connected_distance
 750                    if possible_distance < distance_matrix[connected_id]:
 751                        distance_matrix[connected_id] = possible_distance
 752                        predecessor[connected_id] = current_id
 753                        heappush(open_leaves, (possible_distance, connected_id))
 754
 755        best_dist = float("inf")
 756        best_dest_node = -1
 757        for did, ddist in dest_dict.items():
 758            cand = distance_matrix[did] + ddist
 759            if cand < best_dist:
 760                best_dist = cand
 761                best_dest_node = did
 762
 763        if best_dest_node == -1 or best_dist == float("inf"):
 764            raise Exception(
 765                "Something went wrong, the origin and destination nodes are not connected."
 766            )
 767
 768        return {
 769            "path": self.__reconstruct_path__(best_dest_node, predecessor),
 770            "length": best_dist,
 771        }
 772
 773    @algorithm
 774    def a_star(
 775        self,
 776        origin_id: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float],
 777        destination_id: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float],
 778        heuristic_fn: callable = None,
 779    ) -> dict:
 780        """
 781        Function:
 782
 783        - Identify the shortest path between two nodes in a sparse network graph using an A* extension of Makowski's modified Dijkstra algorithm
 784        - Return a dictionary of various path information including:
 785            - `id_path`: A list of node ids in the order they are visited
 786            - `path`: A list of node dictionaries (lat + long) in the order they are visited
 787
 788        Required Arguments:
 789
 790        - `origin_id`
 791            - Type: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float]
 792            - What: The id of the origin node (or nodes with starting distances) from the graph dictionary to start the shortest path from
 793        - `destination_id`
 794            - Type: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float]
 795            - What: The id of the destination node (or nodes with exit distances) from the graph dictionary to end the shortest path at
 796        - `heuristic_fn`
 797            - Type: function
 798            - What: A heuristic function that takes two node ids and returns an estimated distance between them
 799            - Note: If None, returns the shortest path using Dijkstra's algorithm
 800            - Default: None
 801
 802        Optional Arguments:
 803
 804        - None
 805        """
 806        if heuristic_fn is None:
 807            return self.dijkstra(
 808                origin_id=origin_id,
 809                destination_id=destination_id,
 810            )
 811        # Input Validation
 812        self.__input_check__(origin_id=origin_id, destination_id=destination_id)
 813        origin_dict = normalize_node_input(origin_id)
 814        dest_dict = normalize_node_input(destination_id)
 815
 816        # Variable Initialization
 817        graph = self.graph
 818        distance_matrix = [float("inf")] * len(graph)
 819        visited = [0] * len(graph)
 820        open_leaves = []
 821        predecessor = [-1] * len(graph)
 822
 823        best_dist = float("inf")
 824        best_dest_node = -1
 825        for did, ddist in dest_dict.items():
 826            if did in origin_dict:
 827                cand = origin_dict[did] + ddist
 828                if cand < best_dist:
 829                    best_dist = cand
 830                    best_dest_node = did
 831
 832        def _h(node):
 833            if isinstance(destination_id, int):
 834                return heuristic_fn(node, destination_id)
 835            return min(heuristic_fn(node, did) for did in dest_dict.keys())
 836
 837        for oid, odist in origin_dict.items():
 838            distance_matrix[oid] = odist
 839            heappush(open_leaves, (odist + _h(oid), oid))
 840
 841        while open_leaves:
 842            current_id = heappop(open_leaves)[1]
 843            if distance_matrix[current_id] >= best_dist:
 844                break
 845            if visited[current_id] == 1:
 846                continue
 847            visited[current_id] = 1
 848            current_distance = distance_matrix[current_id]
 849            if current_id in dest_dict:
 850                cand = current_distance + dest_dict[current_id]
 851                if cand < best_dist:
 852                    best_dist = cand
 853                    best_dest_node = current_id
 854            for connected_id, connected_distance in graph[current_id].items():
 855                possible_distance = current_distance + connected_distance
 856                if possible_distance < distance_matrix[connected_id]:
 857                    distance_matrix[connected_id] = possible_distance
 858                    predecessor[connected_id] = current_id
 859                    if connected_id in dest_dict:
 860                        cand = possible_distance + dest_dict[connected_id]
 861                        if cand < best_dist:
 862                            best_dist = cand
 863                            best_dest_node = connected_id
 864                    if possible_distance < best_dist:
 865                        heappush(
 866                            open_leaves,
 867                            (
 868                                possible_distance + _h(connected_id),
 869                                connected_id,
 870                            ),
 871                        )
 872        if best_dest_node == -1 or best_dist == float("inf"):
 873            raise Exception(
 874                "Something went wrong, the origin and destination nodes are not connected."
 875            )
 876
 877        return {
 878            "path": self.__reconstruct_path__(best_dest_node, predecessor),
 879            "length": best_dist,
 880        }
 881
 882    @algorithm
 883    def bellman_ford(
 884        self,
 885        origin_id: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float],
 886        destination_id: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float],
 887    ) -> dict:
 888        """
 889        Function:
 890
 891        - Identify the shortest path between two nodes in a sparse network graph using the Bellman-Ford algorithm
 892        - Return a dictionary of various path information including:
 893            - `id_path`: A list of node ids in the order they are visited
 894            - `path`: A list of node dictionaries (lat + long) in the order they are visited
 895
 896        Required Arguments:
 897
 898        - `origin_id`
 899            - Type: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float]
 900            - What: The id(s) of the origin node(s) (with optional starting distances) from the graph dictionary to start the shortest path from
 901        - `destination_id`
 902            - Type: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float]
 903            - What: The id(s) of the destination node(s) (with optional exit distances) from the graph dictionary to end the shortest path at
 904
 905        Optional Arguments:
 906
 907        - None
 908        """
 909        # Input Validation
 910        self.__input_check__(origin_id=origin_id, destination_id=destination_id)
 911        origin_dict = normalize_node_input(origin_id)
 912        dest_dict = normalize_node_input(destination_id)
 913        graph = self.graph
 914
 915        # Variable Initialization
 916        distance_matrix = [float("inf")] * len(graph)
 917        predecessor = [-1] * len(graph)
 918
 919        for oid, odist in origin_dict.items():
 920            distance_matrix[oid] = odist
 921
 922        len_graph = len(graph)
 923        for i in range(len_graph):
 924            for current_id in range(len(graph)):
 925                current_distance = distance_matrix[current_id]
 926                if current_distance == float("inf"):
 927                    continue
 928                for connected_id, connected_distance in graph[
 929                    current_id
 930                ].items():
 931                    possible_distance = current_distance + connected_distance
 932                    if possible_distance < distance_matrix[connected_id]:
 933                        distance_matrix[connected_id] = possible_distance
 934                        predecessor[connected_id] = current_id
 935                        if i == len_graph - 1:
 936                            raise Exception(
 937                                "Graph contains a negative weight cycle"
 938                            )
 939        best_dist = float("inf")
 940        best_dest_node = -1
 941        for did, ddist in dest_dict.items():
 942            cand = distance_matrix[did] + ddist
 943            if cand < best_dist:
 944                best_dist = cand
 945                best_dest_node = did
 946
 947        if best_dest_node == -1 or best_dist == float("inf"):
 948            raise Exception(
 949                "Something went wrong, the origin and destination nodes are not connected."
 950            )
 951
 952        return {
 953            "path": self.__reconstruct_path__(best_dest_node, predecessor),
 954            "length": best_dist,
 955        }
 956
 957    @algorithm
 958    def bmssp(
 959        self,
 960        origin_id: int | set[int],
 961        destination_id: int,
 962        use_constant_degree_graph: bool = True,
 963    ):
 964        """
 965        Function:
 966
 967        - Identify the shortest path between two nodes in a sparse network graph using the BMSSPy package
 968
 969        - This is now a wrapper for the BMSSPy package
 970            - https://github.com/connor-makowski/bmsspy
 971            - For backwards compatibility, this function wraps around the dijkstra function if BMSSPy is not installed
 972
 973        - Return a dictionary of various path information including:
 974            - `id_path`: A list of node ids in the order they are visited
 975            - `path`: A list of node dictionaries (lat + long) in the order they are visited
 976
 977        Required Arguments:
 978
 979        - `origin_id`
 980            - Type: int | set[int]
 981            - What: The id(s) of the origin node(s) from the graph dictionary to start the shortest path from
 982        - `destination_id`
 983            - Type: int
 984            - What: The id of the destination node from the graph dictionary to end the shortest path at
 985        - `use_constant_degree_graph`
 986            - Type: bool
 987            - What: Whether to convert the graph to a constant degree 2 graph prior to running the BMSSPy algorithm
 988            - Default: True
 989
 990        Optional Arguments:
 991
 992        - None
 993        """
 994        if isinstance(origin_id, (set, dict)) or isinstance(
 995            destination_id, (set, dict)
 996        ):
 997            return self.dijkstra(
 998                origin_id=origin_id, destination_id=destination_id
 999            )
1000        if not hasattr(self, "__bmssp_graph__"):
1001            self.__bmssp_graph__ = Bmssp(
1002                graph=self.graph,
1003                use_constant_degree_graph=use_constant_degree_graph,
1004            )
1005        output = self.__bmssp_graph__.solve(
1006            origin_id=origin_id, destination_id=destination_id
1007        )
1008        return {
1009            "path": output["path"],
1010            "length": output["length"],
1011        }

1013    @algorithm
1014    def cached_shortest_path(
1015        self,
1016        origin_id: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float],
1017        destination_id: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float],
1018        length_only: bool = False,
1019    ):
1020        """
1021        Function:
1022
1023        - Get the shortest path between two nodes in the graph attempting to use a cached shortest path tree if available
1024        - If a cached shortest path tree is not available, it will compute the shortest path tree and cache it for future use if specified by `cache`
1025        - Uses the get_shortest_path_tree (Dijkstra) and get_tree_path functions internally
1026        - Stores cached shortest path trees in a list (self.__cache__) where the index corresponds to the origin node id
1027        - Note: If you modify this graph after caching shortest path trees, the cached trees may become invalid
1028
1029        Required Arguments:
1030
1031        - `origin_id`
1032            - Type: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float]
1033            - What: The id(s) of the origin node(s) (with optional starting distances) from the graph dictionary to start the shortest path from
1034        - `destination_id`
1035            - Type: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float]
1036            - What: The id(s) of the destination node(s) (with optional exit distances) from the graph dictionary to end the shortest path at
1037
1038        Optional Arguments:
1039
1040        - `length_only`
1041            - Type: bool
1042            - What: If True, only returns the length of the path
1043            - Default: False
1044
1045        Returns:
1046
1047        - A dictionary with the following keys:
1048            - `path`: A list of node ids in the order they are visited from the origin node to the destination node
1049            - `length`: The length of the path from the origin node to the destination node
1050        """
1051        # Input Validation
1052        self.__input_check__(origin_id=origin_id, destination_id=destination_id)
1053
1054        # Main function
1055        if isinstance(origin_id, int):
1056            orig_node = origin_id
1057            is_single_origin = True
1058        elif isinstance(origin_id, set) and len(origin_id) == 1:
1059            orig_node = next(iter(origin_id))
1060            is_single_origin = True
1061        elif isinstance(origin_id, dict) and len(origin_id) == 1:
1062            orig_node = next(iter(origin_id.keys()))
1063            is_single_origin = True
1064        else:
1065            is_single_origin = False
1066
1067        if is_single_origin:
1068            if self.__cache__[orig_node] == 0:
1069                self.__cache__[orig_node] = self.get_shortest_path_tree(
1070                    origin_id=orig_node
1071                )
1072            return self.get_tree_path(
1073                origin_id=origin_id,
1074                destination_id=destination_id,
1075                tree_data=self.__cache__[orig_node],
1076                length_only=length_only,
1077            )
1078
1079        res = self.dijkstra(
1080            origin_id=origin_id,
1081            destination_id=destination_id,
1082        )
1083        if length_only:
1084            res["path"] = []
1085        return res

1087    def create_contraction_hierarchy(
1088        self, heuristic_fn=None, ch_graph_kwargs=None, settled_limit: int = 50
1089    ) -> Any:
1090        """
1091        Function:
1092
1093        - Create a Contraction Hierarchies (CH) graph from the current Graph object
1094        - The CH graph is stored as an instance variable `self.__ch_graph__`
1095
1096        Optional Arguments:
1097
1098        - `heuristic_fn`:
1099            - Type: function or None
1100            - What: A heuristic function for CH preprocessing
1101            - Default: None (uses default heuristic)
1102
1103        - `settled_limit`:
1104            - Type: int
1105            - What: The settled count limit for witness search
1106            - Default: 50
1107        """
1108        if not hasattr(self, "__ch_graph__"):
1109            ch_graph_kwargs = (
1110                ch_graph_kwargs if ch_graph_kwargs is not None else dict()
1111            )
1112            self.__ch_graph__ = CHGraph(
1113                graph=self.graph,
1114                inverse_graph=self.inverse_graph,
1115                settled_limit=settled_limit,
1116                heuristic_fn=self.wrap_heuristic(heuristic_fn),
1117                **ch_graph_kwargs,
1118            )
1119        return self.__ch_graph__

1165    @algorithm(bidirectional=True)
1166    def tnr(
1167        self,
1168        origin_id: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float],
1169        destination_id: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float],
1170        length_only: bool = False,
1171        **kwargs,
1172    ) -> dict:
1173        """
1174        Function:
1175
1176        - Perform a Transit Node Routing (TNR) search on the graph
1177        - Automatically creates the TNR hierarchy if it doesn't exist
1178
1179        Required Arguments:
1180
1181        - `origin_id`
1182            - Type: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float]
1183            - What: The id(s) of the origin node(s) (with optional starting distances)
1184        - `destination_id`
1185            - Type: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float]
1186            - What: The id(s) of the destination node(s) (with optional exit distances)
1187
1188        Optional Arguments:
1189
1190        - `length_only`
1191            - Type: bool
1192            - What: If True, only returns the length of the path
1193            - Default: False
1194        """
1195        self.create_tnr_hierarchy(50)
1196        return self.__tnr_graph__.search(
1197            origin_id, destination_id, length_only=length_only
1198        )

1201    def contraction_hierarchy(
1202        self,
1203        origin_id: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float],
1204        destination_id: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float],
1205        length_only: bool = False,
1206    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
1207        """
1208        Function:
1209
1210        - Get the shortest path between two nodes using the Contraction Hierarchies (CH) graph
1211        - Creates the CH graph if it doesn't exist
1212
1213        Requires:
1214
1215        - origin_id: The id(s) of the origin node(s) (with optional starting distances)
1216        - destination_id: The id(s) of the destination node(s) (with optional exit distances)
1217

1219
1220        - length_only: If True, only returns the length of the path
1221
1222        Returns:
1223
1224        - A dictionary with 'path' and 'length' keys containing the shortest path and its length
1225        """
1226        self.create_contraction_hierarchy()
1227        return self.__ch_graph__.search(
1228            origin_id, destination_id, length_only=length_only
1229        )

1232class Graph(
1233    GraphUtils, GraphModifiers, GraphTrees, GraphAlgorithms, GraphReducer
1234):
1235    algorithm = staticmethod(algorithm)
1236
1237    def __init__(self, graph: list[dict[int, int | float]], validate=False):
1238        """
1239        Function:
1240
1241        - Initialize a Graph object
1242        - Validate the input graph
1243
1244        Required Arguments:
1245
1246        - `graph`:
1247            - Type: list of dictionaries with integer keys and integer or float values
1248            - What: A list of dictionaries where the indicies are origin node ids and the values are dictionaries of destination node indices and graph weights
1249            - Note: All nodes must be included as origins in the graph regardless of if they have any connected destinations
1250            - EG:
1251            ```
1252                [
1253                    # From London (index 0)
1254                    {
1255                        # To Paris (index 1)
1256                        1: 311,
1257                    },
1258                    # From Paris (index 1)
1259                    {
1260                        # To London (index 0)
1261                        0: 311,
1262                        # To Berlin (index 2)
1263                        2: 878,

 16    def get_shortest_path_tree(
 17        self,
 18        origin_id: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float],
 19    ) -> dict:
 20        """
 21        Function:
 22
 23        - Calculate the shortest path tree of a graph using Dijkstra's algorithm
 24
 25        Required Arguments:
 26
 27        - `origin_id`
 28            - Type: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float]
 29            - What: The id(s) of the node(s) (with optional starting distances) from which to calculate the shortest path tree
 30
 31        Returns:
 32
 33        - A dictionary with the following keys:
 34            - `origin_id`: The id of the node from which the shortest path tree was calculated
 35            - `predecessors`: A list of node ids referring to the predecessor of each node given the shortest path tree
 36                - Note: For disconnected graphs, nodes that are not connected to the origin node will have a predecessor of None
 37            - `distance_matrix`: A list of distances from the origin node to each node in the graph
 38                - Note: For disconnected graphs, nodes that are not connected to the origin node will have a distance of float("inf")
 39
 40        """
 41        # Input Validation
 42        self.__input_check__(origin_id=origin_id, destination_id=0)
 43        origin_dict = normalize_node_input(origin_id)
 44
 45        # Variable Initialization
 46        graph = self.graph
 47        distance_matrix = [float("inf")] * len(graph)
 48        open_leaves = []
 49        predecessor = [-1] * len(graph)
 50
 51        for oid, odist in origin_dict.items():
 52            distance_matrix[oid] = odist
 53            heappush(open_leaves, (odist, oid))
 54
 55        while open_leaves:
 56            current_distance, current_id = heappop(open_leaves)
 57            for connected_id, connected_distance in graph[current_id].items():
 58                possible_distance = current_distance + connected_distance
 59                if possible_distance < distance_matrix[connected_id]:
 60                    distance_matrix[connected_id] = possible_distance
 61                    predecessor[connected_id] = current_id
 62                    heappush(open_leaves, (possible_distance, connected_id))
 63
 64        return {
 65            "origin_id": origin_id,
 66            "predecessors": predecessor,
 67            "distance_matrix": distance_matrix,
 68        }

 70    def get_tree_path(
 71        self,
 72        origin_id: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float],
 73        destination_id: int,
 74        tree_data: dict,
 75        length_only: bool = False,
 76    ) -> dict:
 77        """
 78        Function:
 79
 80        - Get the path from the origin node to the destination node using the provided tree_data
 81        - Return a list of node ids in the order they are visited as well as the length of the path
 82        - If the destination node is not reachable from the origin node, return None
 83
 84        Required Arguments:
 85
 86        - `origin_id`
 87            - Type: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float]
 88            - What: The id of the origin node from the graph dictionary to start the shortest path from
 89            - Note: Since multiple origins are possible, if the origin_id is not a predecessor node of the destination node, the closest origin will be used.
 90        - `destination_id`
 91            - Type: int
 92            - What: The id of the destination node from the graph dictionary to end the shortest path at
 93        - `tree_data`
 94            - Type: dict
 95            - What: The output from a tree function
 96
 97        Optional Arguments:
 98
 99        - `length_only`
100            - Type: bool
101            - What: If True, only returns the length of the path
102            - Default: False
103
104        Returns:
105
106        - A dictionary with the following keys:
107            - `path`: A list of node ids in the order they are visited from the origin node to the destination node
108            - `length`: The length of the path from the origin node to the destination node
109        """
110        origin_dict = normalize_node_input(origin_id)
111        tree_orig_dict = normalize_node_input(tree_data["origin_id"])
112
113        start_dist = 0.0
114        if len(tree_orig_dict) == 1:
115            tree_root = next(iter(tree_orig_dict.keys()))
116            if tree_root not in origin_dict:
117                raise Exception(
118                    "The origin node must be the same as the spanning node for this function to work."
119                )
120            start_dist = origin_dict[tree_root] - tree_orig_dict[tree_root]
121
122        dest_dict = normalize_node_input(destination_id)
123        best_dist = float("inf")
124        best_dest_node = -1
125        for did, ddist in dest_dict.items():
126            if tree_data["distance_matrix"][did] < float("inf"):
127                tot = start_dist + tree_data["distance_matrix"][did] + ddist
128                if tot < best_dist:
129                    best_dist = tot
130                    best_dest_node = did
131
132        if best_dest_node == -1 or best_dist == float("inf"):
133            raise Exception(
134                "Something went wrong, the origin and destination nodes are not connected."
135            )
136        if length_only:
137            return {"path": [], "length": best_dist}
138        current_id = best_dest_node
139        current_path = [best_dest_node]
140        while current_id != -1 and tree_data["predecessors"][current_id] != -1:
141            current_id = tree_data["predecessors"][current_id]
142            current_path.append(current_id)
143        current_path.reverse()
144        return {
145            "path": current_path,
146            "length": best_dist,
147        }

 151    @algorithm
 152    def dijkstra(
 153        self,
 154        origin_id: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float],
 155        destination_id: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float],
 156    ) -> dict:
 157        """
 158        Function:
 159
 160        - Identify the shortest path between two nodes in a sparse network graph using a modified Dijkstra algorithm
 161
 162        - Return a dictionary of various path information including:
 163            - `path`: A list of node ids in the order they are visited
 164            - `length`: The length of the path from the origin node to the destination node
 165
 166        Required Arguments:
 167
 168        - `origin_id`
 169            - Type: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float]
 170            - What: The id(s) of the origin node(s) (with optional starting distances) from the graph dictionary to start the shortest path from
 171        - `destination_id`
 172            - Type: int | set[int] | dict[int, int | float]
 173            - What: The id(s) of the destination node(s) (with optional exit distances) from the graph dictionary to end the shortest path at
 174
 175        Optional Arguments:
 176
 177        - None
 178        """
 179        # Input Validation
 180        self.__input_check__(origin_id=origin_id, destination_id=destination_id)
 181        origin_dict = normalize_node_input(origin_id)
 182        dest_dict = normalize_node_input(destination_id)
 183
 184        # Variable Initialization
 185        graph = self.graph
 186        distance_matrix = [float("inf")] * len(graph)
 187        predecessor = [-1] * len(graph)
 188        open_leaves = []
 189
 190        for oid, odist in origin_dict.items():
 191            distance_matrix[oid] = odist
 192            heappush(open_leaves, (odist, oid))
 193
 194        best_dist = float("inf")
 195        best_dest_node = -1
 196        for did, ddist in dest_dict.items():
 197            if did in origin_dict:
 198                cand = origin_dict[did] + ddist
 199                if cand < best_dist:
 200                    best_dist = cand
 201                    best_dest_node = did
 202
 203        while open_leaves:
 204            current_distance, current_id = heappop(open_leaves)
 205            if current_distance >= best_dist:
 206                break
 207            if current_distance == distance_matrix[current_id]:
 208                if current_id in dest_dict:
 209                    cand = current_distance + dest_dict[current_id]
 210                    if cand < best_dist:
 211                        best_dist = cand
 212                        best_dest_node = current_id
 213                for connected_id, connected_distance in graph[
 214                    current_id
 215                ].items():
 216                    possible_distance = current_distance + connected_distance
 217                    if possible_distance < distance_matrix[connected_id]:
 218                        distance_matrix[connected_id] = possible_distance
 219                        predecessor[connected_id] = current_id
 220                        if connected_id in dest_dict:
 221                            cand = possible_distance + dest_dict[connected_id]
 222                            if cand < best_dist:
 223                                best_dist = cand
 224                                best_dest_node = connected_id
 225                        if possible_distance < best_dist:
 226                            heappush(
 227                                open_leaves, (possible_distance, connected_id)
 228                            )
 229
 230        if best_dest_node == -1 or best_dist == float("inf"):
 231            raise Exception(
 232                "Something went wrong, the origin and destination nodes are not connected."
 233            )
 234
 235        return {
 236            "path": self.__reconstruct_path__(best_dest_node, predecessor),
 237            "length": best_dist,
 238        }
